Hi Markus — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: for a US mid-market FinTech pilot that needs a fast go-live and wants co-sell support, we usually recommend an AWS Private Offer (Marketplace) as the primary path; direct PO/MSA is the fallback when customers need custom legal terms or on-prem deployment. Below I included a short pros/cons and the action items.

Pros — AWS Private Offer (Marketplace)
- Faster procurement: private offers typically reduce procurement cycles (buyer accepts the private offer vs negotiating an MSA).
- Billing via AWS (consolidated invoice), can be quicker for finance teams already on AWS.
- Co-sell eligibility: we can attach co-sell credit if AWS approves the opportunity.
- Seller of record and tax is handled by AWS/Marketplace contract flow (depends on listing).

Cons — AWS Private Offer
- Co-sell credits and revenue share require an AWS partner motion; timelines vary.
- Some buyers prefer Redwood as seller of record for tax/legal reasons.
- Marketplace refunds/returns follow marketplace policies (less flexible than direct billing).

Pros — Direct PO / MSA
- Full control over contract language, support SLA, and invoicing cadence (monthly/quarterly PO).
- Simpler for customers that require Redwood to be seller of record.
- Easier to accommodate bespoke compliance addendums (e.g., extra audit clauses).

Cons — Direct PO / MSA
- Typically longer legal/Procurement cycles.
- Co-sell with cloud provider may require extra coordination (split credit paths).

Recommended next steps:
1) If you want fastest path to pilot: accept the AWS Private Offer we can put together (I can start the PO template + private offer draft).
2) If BrightLeaf requires Redwood as seller of record or has heavyweight legal terms: we'll run direct PO/MSA — expect 2–4 weeks to finalize on standard terms.
3) I'll loop in Laura (marketplace billing/co-sell) and Rishi (partner credits) to confirm co-sell eligibility and expected timeline.

Attaching a brief draft private offer and a short Q&A doc. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk procurement through it.

Thanks for the summary and for flagging the timeline. My recommendation and rationale below — sending in time for you to respond to BrightLeaf Monday morning.

Recommendation: Proceed with an AWS Private Offer (Marketplace) for pilot, with the following guardrails:
1) Private Offer terms: standard private-offer SKU mapping, buyer accepts on AWS console, billing consolidated to buyer's AWS invoice. We will request co-sell credit with AWS partner sales (Rishi to lead).
2) Legal fallbacks: include a short addendum in the private offer that references our standard MSA (link) and states that a direct PO/MSA will be required only if BrightLeaf needs Redwood as seller-of-record or requires non-standard indemnities. This keeps the procurement path fast but preserves the option to move to direct contract.
3) Billing terms for pilot: offer monthly prepaid for the first 3 months or net-30 invoice (they should choose; clarify in procurement call). Vanessa: please confirm we can accept monthly prepay with startup pricing for pilots.
4) Timeline: we can create the private offer and send to BrightLeaf within 48 hours once they approve pricing; AWS acceptance usually takes 1–3 business days. Co-sell credit approval timeline depends on AWS sales intake; estimate 1–2 weeks.

Action items:
- Rishi: open co-sell request with AWS today and attach the BrightLeaf opportunity id (I can share contact details).
- Vanessa: confirm billing flexibility (monthly prepaid vs net-30) and whether finance needs a specific PO flow.
- Priya: please schedule a 30-min procurement walkthrough with BrightLeaf next week and share the private offer draft.

I'll attach a private_offer_template.pdf for Ops to use. If BrightLeaf pushes for Redwood as seller-of-record, we pivot to direct MSA but set expectations about a longer legal timeline.
